> {quote} The big secret to making bank in this career is... to not expect always to win and keep your risk smaller than your wins. If eu drop below your stop will you continue to hold your hedges until 1.1100 or 1.1000? If you can handle it then you'll deserve the trader of the year award! ![](https://resources.faireconomy.media/images/emojis/64/1f642.png?v=15.1)![](https://resources.faireconomy.media/images/emojis/64/270c-fe0f.png?v=15.1)

Well said!

Not expect always to win - Sometimes we can't take a loss and feel it is a failure (fear). ALSO - Sometimes we can't take a profit because we don't want to lose our position and watch it keep going up after we get out (greed). Plan your trade and trade your plan

Risk smaller than wins - Not to be confused with risk/reward. If you have tested your trading strategies you know they give you the edge.
Conventional wisdom says keep your risk smaller than your reward. Sometimes it is right, especially with untested strategy. But NOT ALWAYS!

Let's say you have a strategy that has a win rate of 85%. You can use a 3/2 risk/reward (r/r) to make this profitable. The extra wins outweighs the larger losses.

Another strategy may have win rate on 10% but the payouts are enormous like 10x or 20x by using long term trend trades. You can use a 1/5 r/r to make this profitable. 1/2 or 1/3 r/r would cut profits too early and make this system a failure.

Always look for the edge, plan your trade and trade your plan. Anything else makes your a gambler.

Happy trades to you,
NB

Excellent! You sound like a very experienced trader. May I ask how do you manage year end tax loss selling to keep the tax consequences low for your trade?

Right now, I have a nice loss in EURUSD longs. With this tremendous bull run in USD I suspect my stop loss at 1.1150 will get taken. But I have booked substantial profits this year and the taxman is going to want a piece, I like to hear what other experienced traders like you and others do in forex to delay taxes?

In a losing year, I will cover some of the losses by cashing in some profitable hedges so as not to waste a huge loss if I don't need to show it. In winning years, I sell my hedges that are showing losses to not show the profits and postpone the tax bill if I don't have expenses to cover the profits. I call it trimming the hedges, lol;-)

I trim the hedges in late December and put the hedges back on in early January unless we have a wild bull/bear run going my way. I like to start the NEW YEAR off with a nice profit.

It's that time of year where taxes becomes important, whether you are only trading EURUSD or if you have other irons in the fire. How do you manage to roll your profits at year end?

Thanks in advance,
